surfaces.part: brown fascia/edge under the roof band

answer.evidence: The cream band at rows 0-2 is a roof/awning top surface. It ends in a brown front-edge line at row 3, with a second brown row at row 4. Rows 5-6 are dark eave shadow (#383c58), and the front wall below runs rows 5-15 (about 11 rows) in purple/blue with a small brown post at x≈11, rows 7-12. The silhouette is a full 16 px wide on every row, so it is a cropped kit cell. The top band is only 3 rows deep and may be cut off by the cell edge, but it still has a front-edge line and shadow, so it is more than a 1-2 row rim.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny sign-like prop, roughly 16x12 source pixels: a cream plank on a purple block with a small brown accent. It is not a whole building with roof, walls and door/windows, so it does not match the reference kind. Its per-tile numbers (11 visible tones, 0% near-flat, 0% neutral dark edge pixels) are on par with the references, but they come from one tiny object. There is no roof-tile scallop, no wall material such as plaster, timber or stone, and no door or window. Each material shows only about 3 shading steps, against 5-6 on the references. Outline pixels are tinted (dark purple/brown), not near-black, which is fine. The piece is far less rich than a full Beodeul building, and as a building it would be much lower in density and structure.

surfaces.part: cream roof/awning band at top of tile
blue-purple front wall with brown post/door frame

answer.evidence: The tile is 16 px wide on every row. Rows 0-2 are a light cream band, read as a roof or awning plane. Row 3 is a lighter brown edge line, row 4 is a darker brown line, and rows 5-6 are dark eave shadow. Rows 7-15 are a vertical blue-purple front wall with a brown post, about 9 rows tall. The top band is cropped by the cell edge and only 3 rows are visible. It still ends in a front-edge line followed by eave shadow, so it counts as a top surface (a) above a front face of more than 3 rows. No isometric side face is drawn.

surfaces.part: cream top band / roof or sign strip
brown edge trim under the band
purple-blue front wall with a brown post

answer.evidence: This is a 16-wide tile fragment. Rows 0-2 are a flat cream band across the full width. Row 3 (#a06234) is a lighter brown edge line, and row 4 is a darker brown line. Rows 5-6 are dark eave shadow (L~56), and rows 5-15 are the front wall in purple-blue with a brown post around x=11. The cream band with an edge line and shadow fits evidence (a), but it is only 3 rows. It could also be read as a face-on framed panel, because a brown frame runs down the left side. The front face is 11 rows. No side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny sign or counter prop, roughly 15x12 source pixels, with a white top slab on a purple-blue base. It is not a whole building: it has no roof, no walls, no door and no windows. The references are full buildings with 5-6 step tile roofs, timber framing and shaded stonework. By eye it is far thinner than a building. It fails because it is the wrong kind of object, and shading depth and structural richness are far below the references.
